record.original_question: Determine whether the gamma_3-flow is nontrivial, that is, whether the induced change of a Poisson bivector is more than a coordinate change along a vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d.

evidence.quote: Recall the standard problem in deformation theory: is the gamma_3-flow nontrivial, i.e. does the change of Poisson bivector not amount to a change of coordinates along a vector field X gamma_3 d on R d ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma_3$ denote the Kontsevich tetrahedral graph cocycle (the smallest nontrivial cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex of unoriented graphs), and let $P$ be a Poisson bivector on $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. a bivector field $P=\tfrac12 P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i\wedge\partial_j$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ (Schouten bracket). Using the Kontsevich graph orientation morphism, the cocycle $\Gamma_3$ produces a bivector $Q_{\Gamma_3}(P)=\mathcal{O}r(\Gamma_3)(P)$ that is a Poisson cocycle: $[\![P,Q_{\Gamma_3}(P)]\!]=0$. This defines the $\Gamma_3$-flow $\dot P = Q_{\Gamma_3}(P)$ on the space of Poisson structures.

The flow is called trivial at $P$ if there exists a vector field $X_{\Gamma_3}^d$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (depending on $P$) such that
$$Q_{\Gamma_3}(P) \;=\; [\![P,\, X_{\Gamma_3}^d]\!],$$
i.e. the infinitesimal deformation is realized by a change of coordinates (a Poisson coboundary). Otherwise the flow is called nontrivial.

Problem: Determine whether the $\Gamma_3$-flow is nontrivial, that is, decide whether there exists a Poisson bivector $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for some $d$) for which $Q_{\Gamma_3}(P)$ is not of the form $[\![P, X]\!]$ for any vector field $X$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Poisson deformations
artifact.status_search_result: The nontriviality of the Kontsevich tetrahedral $\Gamma_3$-flow on general Poisson structures is described as an open problem in the deformation-theory literature: no example of a Poisson bracket on which the $\Gamma_3$-flow produces a genuinely inequivalent (non-coordinate-equivalent) deformation has been found. Recent work has established triviality (Poisson coboundary) in special classes — e.g., the $\Gamma_3$-flow on Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets over $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the tetrahedral flow in 4D — but the general nontriviality question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Standard problem in deformation theory: is the gamma_3-flow nontrivial, i.e. does the change of Poisson bivector not amount to a change of coordinates along a vector field.
status_evidence.claim: The nontriviality of the gamma_3-flow is listed as a standard open problem in deformation theory.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: The tetrahedral flow is a Poisson coboundary in 4D for Nambu-determinant brackets.
status_evidence.claim: In specific dimensions/classes the gamma_3-flow has been shown to be a coboundary (trivial), but the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket.
status_evidence.claim: Finding a Poisson bracket on which the graph cocycle action (in particular gamma_3) is nontrivial is an open problem.
